title: DNA Match Contact Response Rate
dataSources: Tree records (`genealogy:record`), DNA matches (`dna:match`), ancestor events (`ancestor:event`), archive documents (`archive:document`), tree nodes (`familytree:node`).
app: Genealogy and family-history research — tree platforms (Ancestry, FamilySearch), DNA match exports (23andMe, MyHeritage), and document / archive catalogues — streamed to Splunk HEC via GEDCOM and CSV exports.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=dna:match contacted=yes
| stats sum(eval(if(response_received="yes",1,0))) as responses, count as contacts by testing_service
| eval response_pct=round(100*responses/contacts,1)
| sort - response_pct
description: Measures how often outreach to DNA matches actually produces a response on each testing platform.
value: Contact time is limited, and a platform-level response rate helps prioritize where outreach is worth doing.
implementation: Track outreach and response state in `dna:match`; calculate response percentage by testing service.
visualization: Table of DNA services with contact response percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It logs where messages to DNA matches are most likely to get a reply.
